what: Lab B26 (scripts/50_rocket_moonshine_enc.sh): Moonshine Tiny encoder, int8 via ModelBlaster (patches/0100), on Rocket hart 0 of the PYNQ-Z1. MEASURED rdcycle counts on the board.

roccmoon_0x5A5A0010.command: ROCCMOON_ACCEPTED=7475c1b20b34f42e3bbe192f41cee58f scripts/with_board.sh ./scripts/50_rocket_moonshine_enc.sh --board-only --name rocket_moonshine_enc_roccmoon --variants "nl ew nl_eng ew_eng" --stems "" --board chipyard_pynqz1_micrgb --bit fpga/pynq-z2/build_rocket_micrgb_roccmoon_z1/pynqz1_rocket_micrgb_roccmoon.bit --magic 0x5A5A0010 --runner run_rocket_roccmoon.py
notes: One session, one bitstream: the engine variants (nl_eng, ew_eng) and their MBP twins (nl, ew, ew_bigconv) and the control image before and after.

Engine runtime as of the images' build (2026-09-17 00:17, before commits 05c5416 and 6e6f5ec): byte-wise result placement on hart 1, image cache keyed (address, kind). Moonshine has one const weight array per layer, so the cache-key bug does not reach it; the goldens matching exactly on the board agrees.

The encoder images run NO warm-up (MB_WARMUP=0) and ITERS=1: every number is ONE cold inference. The engine's one-time weight-image build (mbxr_rt_stats.image_cycles) is therefore inside its measured linear/conv dispatches; engine_vs_twin gives totals with and without that measured counter.

enc_ew runs pext_patch_dot8 at its default limits, which send conv3 (IC*KH=576 > 512 rows) to the scalar reference although kernel_picks.json names pext_patch_dot8; enc_ew_bigconv is the same generated C with -DMB_PEXT_CONV_MAXROWS=2048 -DMB_PEXT_CONV_WBYTES=2097152 and is the fair MBP twin for conv2d_s8.
max_abs_err is against each image's own baked host-C golden (the same generated C compiled for the host against pext.h's software model of MBP), not against the Python golden.
RTF = dispatch cycles / 34,482,759 Hz / 4.0 s of audio (encoder only; no front end, no decoder).
Mic bitstream (no engine): nl and ew encoders, ew_bigconv, the stem layout lever (time on W vs time on H) at default and raised conv limits, control image before and after.
Encoder images: same MB_WARMUP=0 / ITERS=1 and host-C golden conventions as the roccmoon session. Stem images DO run a warm-up (MB_WARMUP=1); their timed run is within 0.03 % of it.

pext_patch_dot8 takes its DOT8 path only if IC*KH <= MB_PEXT_CONV_MAXROWS (default 512). Time on W: conv3 (IC*KH = 576) is scalar. Time on H: conv2 (288*7 = 2016) and conv3 (576*3 = 1728) are scalar. The *_bigconv images raise the limit so every conv is on DOT8; the default-limit ratio mostly measures which convolutions fall back, the bigconv ratio measures the layout.

todo_items_4_and_5b_from_the_graph.item_4_depthwise: does not apply: no depthwise_conv2d_s8 op; the three convolutions are dense (Conv2d groups=1: 1->288, 288->576, 576->288).
todo_items_4_and_5b_from_the_graph.item_5b_short_reductions: does not apply: conv reduction lengths K = IC*KH*KW are 127, 2016 and 1728; the shortest dot product anywhere is matmul_b_s8 q.k at K = 36 (head dim 288/8), then linear K = 288 / 1152 and matmul_b a.v K = 165. None is below 32.

ram_read_caveat: peek_ram.py reads DRAM behind Rocket's caches; a recently written line can read stale (ctrl_ffn cyc[0] read 0 ten seconds after the console printed its value). Non-zero = written; zero = unknown.
